done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (anything the app's date reader parses, such as last 30 days, explicit dates and date ranges, plus a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: The year/amount heuristic still rejects ordinary terse year wording. For example, `Show Actuals 2025` on a follow-up does not parse as calendar year 2025: `hasAmountContext` sees `Actuals` before the number and makes `calendarYear` skip it. The service then treats the question as having no period, clears the model's window, and inherits the prior window instead. Thus a prior July answer remains July even though the follow-up explicitly names 2025. This is distinct new evidence from the coordinator's ruling preserving `Actual to 2025` and `Actual of 2025`; neither ruled phrase is involved.
findings.title: Not done: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (anything the app's date reader parses, such as last 30 days, explicit dates

findings.body: A clear amount phrase such as `Show an amount totalling to 2025` is still converted to calendar year 2025. Although `amount` and `totalling` are amount words, `hasAmountContext` returns false because the text immediately before the number ends in `to`; the comparison guard does not match `totalling to`, so `calendarYear` accepts 2025 and overwrites the model/prior window. This is new evidence not covered by the ruling that preserves the shorter `Actual to 2025` calendar-year behavior.
findings.title: Not done: an amount is never read as a year

findings.body: The new matrix and rerun checks still call `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`, where the LLM, executor/warehouse, audit, dimensions, reports, and resolver are fakes. The frontend period-control tests also mock the API, and the registered test command contains no Playwright/browser suite. Consequently, named-period precedence, inheritance/aggregation, amount protection, and changing an answer's period have no required end-to-end proof through a browser, running API, real database, and user flow. The successful close run only exercised these service/jsdom boundaries, so the prior test-audit blocker remains open.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
